interpretation: Chromium directly attributed 435.583 ms of the fresh launch to background parsing of the workbench module. In the separate warmed launch it accepted an 11,685,400-byte code cache for that module and no corresponding background-parse event appeared. Parse, evaluation, and cache events can overlap other startup work and must not be added to the workbench-import duration. With the faster warmed renderer, the shell-environment promise resolved 270 ms after local host allocation, making it a plausible extension-host gate. On the cold launch the promise resolved 6 ms before allocation, so that gate was absent. These are raw renderer CDP marks, not an exact main-process shell-completion or utilityProcess.fork timestamp. One run of each profile condition does not estimate a reliable speed difference or p95.
perfviewCaveat: The Startup Performance report labeled both launches cached data: NO. Its label is a heuristic based on the configured code-cache path and last-running commit, not direct evidence of Chromium module-cache use; the warmed Chromium compile event explicitly reports cacheRejected=false.
